42951718.text: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) are heterogeneous autoimmune disorders that affect skeletal muscle and may involve the skin, lungs, heart, gastrointestinal tract, or be associated with malignancy. Imaging supports phenotyping, biopsy targeting, assessment of disease burden, and monitoring. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains the principal modality for muscle assessment, depicting edema, fascial and subcutaneous inflammation, fatty replacement, and atrophy without ionizing radiation. Whole-body MRI maps disease distribution, whereas quantitative techniques, including Dixon fat-fraction imaging and T2 mapping, provide objective measures of activity and chronic damage. Ultrasound offers a portable, inexpensive adjunct, although operator dependence and limited standardization restrict comprehensive assessment. For nuclear medicine, 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT provides a complementary whole-body measure of metabolism, potentially identifying muscle inflammation, interstitial lung disease, other systemic manifestations, and occult malignancy in selected patients. Physiologic muscle uptake and heterogeneous acquisition and quantification protocols limit specificity and prevent universal PET thresholds. Hybrid PET/MRI combines metabolic and structural characterization, but evidence supporting routine use remains limited. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET is an emerging pathway-targeted approach with preliminary evidence in muscle and myositis-associated lung disease. This review summarizes imaging patterns across major myositis phenotypes, contrasts established and investigational uses of MRI, ultrasound, FDG PET/CT, PET/MRI, and emerging tracers, illustrates important mimics and pitfalls, and proposes a practical multimodality imaging approach.

43020618.text: It has been hypothesized that effective cellular internalization is required for the retention of 225Ac daughter radionuclides. Both the complex decay chain of 225Ac and the recoil-mediated release of daughters, particularly 213Bi (half-life, 46 min), raise concerns about redistribution that may reduce tumor absorbed dose (TAD) and increase off-target radiation exposure. Because somatostatin receptor subtype 2 antagonists, such as satoreotide tetraxetan (SSO110, also known as DOTA-JR11), are not internalized, it has been proposed that the daughter radionuclides are less effectively retained compared with internalizing agonists, such as DOTATATE. In this study, we performed a direct and quantitative comparison of daughter radionuclide redistribution after administration of [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 and [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Methods: Biodistribution and 213Bi redistribution were evaluated in BALB/c nude mice bearing NCI-H69 small cell lung cancer xenografts. Repeated γ-counting combined with biexponential modeling was used to quantify 225Ac and 213Bi activity in tumors, blood, bone marrow, kidneys, the liver, and the intestines up to 96 h postinjection. TAD was calculated with and without accounting for experimentally derived 213Bi redistribution. Real-time in vitro binding assays were conducted to characterize cellular retention of [225Ac]Ac-SSO110. Results: [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 demonstrated higher tumor uptake and prolonged retention compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution of 213Bi from tumors was minimal and comparable between the agonist and antagonist and reduced the TAD by 4.5% for [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 and 3.9% for [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. After accounting for this redistribution, [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 delivered a 2.8-fold higher TAD and a 1.8-fold higher tumor-to-kidney absorbed dose (AD) ratio compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Moreover, 213Bi redistribution had no relevant impact on AD estimates in evaluated healthy organs, including the kidneys, the intestines, blood, and bone marrow. Real-time binding studies demonstrated a sustained cell-associated β--signal after incubation with [225Ac]Ac-SSO110. Conclusion: Despite negligible internalization, [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 did not show increased macroscopic 213Bi redistribution compared with the internalizing agonist [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution was limited for both radiopeptides and had only a minor effect on AD estimates for tumors and the evaluated healthy tissues. [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 achieved a higher TAD and more favorable tumor-to-kidney ratio compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Overall, these findings support further evaluation of antagonist-based 225Ac radiopharmaceutical therapy.

43026718.label: Background
43026718.text: Kidney injury during metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progression remains incompletely characterized.

43026718.label: Purpose
43026718.text: To assess multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) for early detection and monitoring of MASLD-associated kidney injury.

43026718.label: Animal model
43026718.text: Fifty male Sprague Dawley rats received high-fat diet plus very low-dose carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) underwent mpMRI before sacrifice at 0, 2, 4, 8, or 12 weeks (n = 10/time point). Ten MASLD and ten normal rats underwent serial MRI at each time point; ten CCl4-only rats served as nephrotoxicity controls. Twelve additional healthy rats underwent a scan-rescan test.

43026718.label: Field strength/sequence
43026718.text: 3 T; turbo spin-echo T2-weighted imaging, variable flip angle (VFA) gradient-echo T1 mapping, multi-echo gradient-echo blood oxygen level-dependent imaging, pulsed arterial spin labeling, echo-planar diffusion kurtosis imaging, and multi-echo Dixon imaging.

43026718.label: Assessment
43026718.text: Two radiologists (5 and 13 years of experience) quantified T1, T2*, proton density fat fraction (PDFF), mean diffusivity, mean kurtosis (MK), and renal blood flow (RBF) in cortex, outer/inner stripes of outer medulla (OSOM/ISOM). Early injury was defined as a tubular injury score ≥ 2. Histopathology, immunohistochemistry, transcriptomics, and serum metabolomics were performed.

43026718.label: Statistical tests
43026718.text: Repeated-measures ANOVA; intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). p < 0.05 indicated significance.

43026718.label: Results
43026718.text: Scan-rescan ICCs were 0.682-0.876. OSOM MK/PDFF significantly increased by Week 2 [MK (×10-3): 0.532 ± 0.007 to 0.574 ± 0.004; PDFF (%): 2.489 ± 0.243 to 3.600 ± 0.347]; cortical RBF and OSOM T2* showed no significant changes at Week 2 (p = 0.786, 1.000) but significantly decreased from Week 4. OSOM MK/PDFF had AUCs of 0.952 and 0.905 for early renal injury. Multi-omics revealed inflammatory and lipid/bile acid alterations. Dodecanedioic/hippuric acids potentially linked MASLD severity to OSOM MK.

43026718.label: Data conclusion
43026718.text: Renal mpMRI detected early kidney injury during MASLD progression.

43043468.label: Purpose
43043468.text: This study evaluated the performance of liver and spleen stiffness measurement (LSM and SSM) by two-dimensional shear-wave elastography (2D-SWE) in ruling out high-risk esophageal varices (HRVs) and their utility in predicting other portal hypertension-related gastroduodenal lesions and liver-related events (LREs) in patients with cirrhosis.

43043468.label: Materials and methods
43043468.text: This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive adult patients with cirrhosis undergoing screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) between 2023 and 2025 at Chulalongkorn University Hospital, Thailand. LSM and SSM were acquired using 2D-SWE (Supersonic Mach 30) within 2 days of EGD by a single blinded operator. HRVs were defined endoscopically as medium-to-large varices or small varices with red wale markings.

43043468.label: Results
43043468.text: 169 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled. Of these, 77 (45.6%) and 40 (23.7%) patients had esophageal varices (EVs) and HRVs, respectively. Leading cirrhosis causes were hepatitis B and C virus (n = 66, 39.1%). At thresholds to maximize specificity while maintaining sensitivity ≥ 90%, LSM < 13.7 kPa and SSM < 37.6 kPa by 2D-SWE could spare EGD in 36.7% and 44.4%, respectively, with corresponding missed HRV rates of 4.8% and 4%. Moreover, 2D-SWE-derived LSM and SSM yielded AUCs of 0.778 and 0.844 for HRVs, 0.742 and 0.785 for EVs, and 0.766 and 0.724 for portal hypertensive gastropathy (all p < 0.001). In multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis, Child-Pugh score and LSM by 2D-SWE were independently associated with the development of LREs within 1 year.

43043468.label: Conclusion
43043468.text: LSM and SSM using 2D-SWE may help reduce the need for screening EGD in patients with cirrhosis, with observed missed-HRV rates of 4.8% and 4.0%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of 2D-SWE for variceal risk stratification, particularly where vibration-controlled transient elastography is unavailable. The proposed cutoffs require external validation before clinical implementation.

43066668.label: Background
43066668.text: Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized.

43066668.label: Objectives
43066668.text: The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals.

43066668.label: Methods
43066668.text: A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement.

43066668.label: Results
43066668.text: A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis.

43066668.label: Conclusions
43066668.text: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

43071018.label: Objectives
43071018.text: Sarcopenia and visceral fat obesity (VFO) are risk factors for adverse postoperative outcomes in colorectal cancer (CRC). This study investigated perioperative changes in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue in CRC patients and their predictive value for long-term survival.

43071018.label: Materials and methods
43071018.text: This cohort study enrolled stage I-III CRC patients who received upfront curative resection. Pre- and postoperative CT scans were obtained to quantify the skeletal muscle index (SMI) for sarcopenia assessment and the visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR) for VFO assessment. Landmark analyses were performed at 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Overall survival (OS) was set as the primary survival endpoint.

43071018.label: Results
43071018.text: A total of 266 patients (median [interquartile range, IQR] age, 55 [50-62] years; 156 males) were included. Landmark Cox regression analyses showed that sarcopenia at baseline and 3 months postoperatively was an independent risk factor for OS (hazard ratio [HR]: 3.408, p = 0.001; HR: 2.497, p = 0.016). VFO at baseline and 3 months postoperatively correlated with poorer OS in the univariable analysis (HR: 1.803, p = 0.026; HR: 1.905, p = 0.030). Integrated prediction models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.799 at baseline and 0.774 at 3 months postoperatively for OS.

43071018.label: Conclusion
43071018.text: Sarcopenia at baseline and 3 months postoperatively is an independent risk factor for inferior OS, whereas VFO is associated with poorer OS only at the univariable level. Combining perioperative sarcopenia and VFO with clinical factors could assist in the prognostic stratification for stage I-III CRC patients following surgical resection.

43071018.label: Key points
43071018.text: Question The prognostic influence of perioperative changes in CT-derived skeletal muscle and adipose tissues on colorectal cancer survival remains unclear. Findings Sarcopenia and VFO at baseline and the 3-month postoperative landmark are associated with worse overall survival and add incremental prognostic value to conventional clinical risk indicators. Critical relevance statement This work highlights the prognostic value of perioperative CT-derived sarcopenia and VFO for stage I-III CRC, suggesting that opportunistic body composition assessment on routine surveillance scans could provide valuable insights for future clinical risk stratification and management strategies.

43076968.label: Background
43076968.text: To evaluate total and selected (regions 2 and 9-12) CT‑based and PET‑based Peritoneal Cancer Index (CT‑PCI and PET‑PCI) for predicting surgical resectability and overall survival (OS) in pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP).

43076968.label: Methods
43076968.text: 54 patients were retrospectively enrolled. The predictive performance of total and selected CT-PCI and PET-PCI for surgical resectability was assessed using ROC curve analysis. OS was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, with comparisons stratified by CT-PCI, PET-PCI, and completeness of cytoreduction (CCR) scores. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify independent prognostic factors.

43076968.label: Results
43076968.text: CT-PCI demonstrated high predictive accuracy for resectability (total: 92.6%; selected: 90.7%), whereas PET-PCI showed moderate to high accuracy (total: 74.1%; selected: 88.8%). Patients with high total or selected CT-PCI or PET-PCI scores had worse OS than those with low scores (all log-rank P < 0.001). Significant OS differences were also observed between CCR subgroups: CCR 0-1 versus CCR 3 (P = 0.04), CCR 0-1 versus CCR 4 (P < 0.001), and CCR 2 versus CCR 4 (P = 0.011). Notably, OS didn't differ significantly between CCR 3 (incomplete cytoreduction) and CCR 4 (no surgery). Multivariate Cox regression identified both CT-PCI (HR = 5.589, P = 0.033) and PET-PCI (HR = 6.992, P = 0.007) as independent prognostic factors for OS.

43076968.label: Conclusion
43076968.text: Both total and selected CT-PCI and PET-PCI are useful for predicting resectability and OS in PMP patients. CT-PCI is more suitable for preoperative resectability assessment, whereas PET-PCI provides complementary prognostic information. Selected PCI (regions 2 and 9-12) showed predictive performance comparable to that of total PCI while requiring assessment of fewer regions.

43086118.label: Background
43086118.text: ChemoHormonal Therapy Versus Androgen Ablation Randomized Trial for Extensive Disease in Prostate Cancer (CHAARTED) risk stratification is an important risk stratification tool in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). However, clinicians are increasingly using prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography (PSMA-PET)/computed tomography (CT).

43086118.label: Objective
43086118.text: Here, the prognostic value of PSMA-total tumor volume (PSMA-TTV) for overall survival (OS) in a developmental cohort from the Enzalutamide in First-Line Androgen Deprivation Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer (ENZAMET) trial with validation in the larger Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) Registry was evaluated.

43086118.label: Design, setting, and participants
43086118.text: Participants who underwent PSMA-PET/CT before enrolment in the prospective phase 3 ENZAMET trial (development cohort) or were classified as having mHSPC in the ongoing international PROMISE Registry (validation cohort) were included, and PSMA-TTV was derived using a semiautomated method. In the ENZAMET dataset, the association of PSMA-TTV categories with time to progression and OS in addition to CHAARTED groups by conventional imaging, was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests. ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV categories were tested in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests and Cox regression analyses.

43086118.label: Results and limitations
43086118.text: Overall, 100 patients from ENZAMET and 993 patients from the PROMISE Registry were analyzed. The upper ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV category was ≥72 ml. In patients with CHAARTED criteria low-volume disease, 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml versus <72 ml was 36% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 16-83) versus 71% (60-85; p = 0.019) in survival curves; 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml was not associated with shorter OS in the ENZAMET subgroup (50% [32-78] vs 73% [63-85]; p = 0.063) but in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup (33% [27-40] vs 78% [75-81]; p < 0.001). The hazard ratio for upper PSMA-TTV category ≥72 ml was 6.8 (95% CI = 5.3-8.7) in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup.

43086118.label: Conclusions
43086118.text: PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml from an ENZAMET cohort is prognostic for OS in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort. Further validation of PSMA-TTV as a prognostic biomarker with potential to be a predictive marker to identify patients for intensification is warranted.
